source.author: verg
source.text: Ego te, quae plurima fando enumerare vales, numquam, regina, negabo promeritam; nec me meminisse pigebit Elissae, dum memor ipse mei, dum spiritus hos regit artus.
source.text_original: 'Ego te, quae plurima fando / enumerare vales, numquam, regina, negabo / promeritam; nec me meminisse pigebit Elissae, / dum memor ipse mei, dum spiritus hos regit artus.
source.text_english: I shall never deny, queen, that you have well earned my gratitude, you who can recount so many things in speaking; nor shall I ever be ashamed to remember Elissa, so long as I myself remember myself, so long as breath rules these limbs.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Caeterum post sanctae Paulae dormitionem, cujus vita virtutis exemplum est, et hos libros, quos Eustochio virgini Christi negare non potui, decrevimus, dum spiritus hos regit artus, Prophetarum explanationi incumbere, et omissum jamdiu opus, quodam postliminio repetere: praesertim cum et admirabilis sanctusque vir Pammachius hoc idem litteris flagitet, et nos ad patriam festinantes, mortiferos Sirenarum cantus surda debeamus aure transire.
reuse.text_original: Caeterum post sanctae Paulae dormitionem, cujus vita virtutis exemplum est, et hos libros, quos Eustochio virgini Christi negare non potui, decrevimus, dum spiritus hos regit artus, Prophetarum explanationi incumbere, et omissum jamdiu opus, quodam postliminio repetere: praesertim cum et admirabilis sanctusque vir Pammachius hoc idem litteris flagitet, et nos ad patriam festinantes, mortiferos Sirenarum cantus surda debeamus aure transire.
reuse.text_english: But after the repose of holy Paula, whose life is an example of virtue, and after these books, which I could not refuse to Eustochium the virgin of Christ, we have resolved, while spirit still guides these limbs, to devote ourselves to the explanation of the Prophets, and to take up again, as it were by a right of return, a work long since laid aside; especially since the admirable and holy man Pammachius is urging the same thing in letters, and we, hurrying to our homeland, ought to pass by the deadly songs of the Sirens with deaf ear.
